artifacts_audited.description: L2-EXP-11 Adaptive q10 NN Relaxation Evaluation

section_1_causal_pairs_and_provenance.station_name: Mount Nuolja Automatic Weather Station (Middle Station)
section_1_causal_pairs_and_provenance.nwp_source: MET Norway MEPS 18Z run (grid point y=760, x=486; 1.24 km offset)

provenance_gaps.finding: 2020-2023 Historical MEPS extraction only spans hours 00:00 to 18:00 UTC (19 hours per origin). Target hours 19:00 to 23:00 UTC are 100% absent across all 1,369 historical origins.

Inconsistent horizon indexing: 1,321 origins are indexed h=1..19 (dispatch hour + 1), while 48 recovered origins are indexed h=6..24 (MEPS lead time). Consequently, horizons 20-24 have zero daytime rows in 2022 validation and only 20 daytime rows in 2023 blind test.

Absence of direct/diffuse radiation decomposition: Nuolja AWS has only a single unshaded upward pyranometer (SW_IN). No DNI, DHI, downward shortwave, or surface optical albedo exist anywhere in the repository (EXP-06).
Absence of sensor calibration records: No calibration certificates, sensitivity multipliers, cosine error curves, leveling checks, or maintenance/cleaning logs exist for the pyranometer (EXP-06).

section_3_error_characteristics.heteroscedasticity: VERIFIED — Error standard deviation ranges from ~9 W/m² (horizon 1) to ~106 W/m² (horizon 12), and from 13.9 W/m² (solar elevation < 5 deg) to 132.0 W/m² (> 35 deg). Error spread is non-stationary.
section_3_error_characteristics.asymmetry_and_bias: VERIFIED — Candidate F exhibits systematic over-prediction bias during daytime (+29.15 W/m² in 2020-2023 historical, up to +22.45 W/m² in afternoon 2024). Downside errors cause critical microgrid deficits.

horizon_autocorrelation.findings: Strong adjacent-horizon correlation: r(h6,h7)=0.78, r(h7,h8)=0.63, r(h11,h12)=0.63, r(h12,h13)=0.70, r(h13,h14)=0.69. Cloud forecast errors persist over 3 to 6 hours rather than acting as independent noise.

day_to_day_persistence.finding: 21.5% of next day's forecast origin residual is linearly predictable from the previous day's residual.

authoritative_requalification_results.methodological_firewall_note: These authoritative one-sided q10 requalification figures (nominal 90%) must NOT be conflated with the L2 conformal prediction interval experiments (L2-EXP-01/02/03), which evaluated two-sided 80% intervals [q10, q90] under Stage C physical bounding (1.25 * clearsky_ghi) that collapsed to 70.0%-71.8%.

section_4_static_q10_evaluation.reliability_benefit_verified: In L2-EXP-07, planning against static q10 cut realized critical unmet load by 93.39% (7,994 Wh/origin to 529 Wh/origin, p=8.75e-20).
section_4_static_q10_evaluation.operational_cost_verified: In L2-EXP-07, static q10 increased diesel fuel by +38.18% (+16.36 L/origin, +2,012 L total) and increased solar curtailment by +92.87% (+34.7 kWh/origin, +4.26 MWh total) across 123 NORMAL origins.
section_4_static_q10_evaluation.nature_of_2023_calibration_failure: The 2023 calibration failure is not a catastrophic statistical collapse, but a mild seasonal under-coverage drift (86.77% vs 87.00% floor). The disqualifying operational defect of static q10 is that enforcing a 90% lower bound at every single hour of every 24h horizon is economically ruinous (+38.2% fuel, +92.9% curtailment), treating crystal-clear midday sun with identical conservatism as storm fronts.

relaxation_failure_mechanisms.pointwise_adaptive_nn_exp_11: Pointwise uncoordinated relaxation (EXP-11) doubled unmet load (+106.3%) because morning optimism suppressed diesel, causing battery exhaustion during afternoon cloud troughs.
relaxation_failure_mechanisms.horizon_risk_budget_exp_12: Hourly budget decay without joint state integration (EXP-12) worsened unmet load to 111.2 kWh (+71.0% over static q10).

static_quantile.justification: Fails empirical calibration in 2023; incurs +38% fuel penalty and +93% curtailment.

horizon_dependent_quantiles.justification: Horizons 20-24 have zero daytime rows in 2022 validation in the 2020-2023 archive; cannot learn horizon-dependent adjustments for full 24h cycle.

prediction_intervals.justification: Stage B unconstrained CQR achieves 80.4% coverage, but Stage C physical bounding drops to 70.05% because setting a diffuse floor constant is blocked by lack of DHI/DNI sensors (EXP-06).

residual_distributions.justification: Directly computable from 26,011 rows (2020-2023) and 2,216 rows (2024); preserves heteroscedasticity, regimes, and empirical asymmetry.

scenarios.justification: HiGHS MILP solves 3 scenarios in 1.5s (EXP-09/10), but non-anticipativity and priority semantics must be preserved, and scenarios must be trajectory-coherent rather than marginal quantiles.

cumulative_horizon_error_bounds.justification: Battery storage is an energy integrator (Wh). Total 24h energy error (mean +24 Wh/m2, std 530 Wh/m2, q10 -608 Wh/m2) matches microgrid physical failure mechanisms far better than hourly pointwise margins.

lumped_24h_energy_bound.definition: Single scalar energy error bound over full 24h: sum_{t=1}^{24} (y_pred - y_true) * dt
lumped_24h_energy_bound.empirical_limitation: In 97.7% of evaluated 2024 origins, the maximum cumulative solar shortfall occurs BEFORE horizon 24 (peaking at horizons 14-17). Mean maximum intra-day cumulative shortfall is 227.2 Wh/m2, compared to a final 24h net shortfall of only 24.0 Wh/m2 (nearly 10x difference).
lumped_24h_energy_bound.physical_flaw: Battery storage is an energy integrator that responds to cumulative energy at time k (E_k). If solar is over-predicted from 09:00 to 14:00 UTC, the battery depletes and triggers afternoon unmet load before hour 24. A lumped 24h bound cannot protect against intra-day drawdown timing.

prefix_cumulative_error_bound.definition: Monotonically structured cumulative error bound over prefixes k in [1..24]: Delta E_prefix(k) = sum_{t=1}^k (y_pred - y_true) * dt
prefix_cumulative_error_bound.empirical_support: Empirical prefix error spread std(E_prefix(k)) grows continuously from 3.7 Wh/m2 at h=1 to 511.4 Wh/m2 at h=16, then plateaus at night (h >= 18). Peak 90th percentile prefix shortfall reaches 692.2 Wh/m2 at h=18.
prefix_cumulative_error_bound.operational_fit: Aligns exactly with receding-horizon dispatch and battery state trajectory E_k >= E_min + Delta E_prefix(k). Directly prevents the afternoon battery exhaustion observed in EXP-11 and EXP-12.

what_we_know: Solar forecast error is non-stationary, heteroscedastic, and scales with solar elevation and cloud cover.
Candidate F has an empirical positive daytime bias (+2.5 to +29.2 W/m2) that leads unbuffered EMS into energy deficits.
Solar forecast errors have strong temporal autocorrelation across adjacent horizons (r=0.63 to 0.78) and day-to-day persistence (r=0.464, R2=21.5%).
Planning against static q10 cuts unmet critical load by 93.4%, but at an operational penalty of +38.2% diesel fuel and +92.9% solar curtailment.

Authoritative q10 requalification confirms nominal 90% coverage achieved 90.12% in 2022 validation, 86.77% in 2023 blind test (failing the [87%, 93%] acceptance band by 0.23%), and 88.53% pooled. Static q10 is therefore marginally calibrated, but operationally over-conservative (+38.2% fuel, +92.9% curtailment).
Uncoordinated pointwise hourly relaxation of q10 (EXP-11, EXP-12) fails because morning optimism empties the battery before afternoon deficit troughs.
what_we_do_not_know: True decomposition of low-sun irradiance into diffuse skylight, terrain albedo, and sensor cosine error (blocked by lack of DHI/DNI at Nuolja AWS).
True physical fuel consumption in Liters (blocked by prototype linear fuel equation; no bench calibration).
Performance on hours 19:00 to 23:00 UTC across 2020-2023 (blocked by MEPS 18Z +24h lead time cutoff).
Closed-loop performance under live rolling-horizon operational telemetry (only semi-empirical replay on 173 odd origins has been tested).
final_synthesis.why_static_q10_is_not_defensible: Static q10 is not defensible as an operational uncertainty representation because: (1) while its one-sided calibration is near nominal (90.12% in 2022, 88.53% pooled), it suffered a confirmed 2023 blind test failure (86.77% vs 87% floor), (2) applying a 10th-percentile derating uniformly across all 24 hours ignores the strong 9x variance expansion between dawn and midday, (3) it imposes an economically prohibitive penalty of +38.18% diesel fuel and +92.87% solar curtailment by assuming storm conditions during clear midday sun, and (4) its reliability benefit is achieved through brute-force fossil over-generation rather than genuine uncertainty awareness.
final_synthesis.single_best_uncertainty_representation_t: Prefix Cumulative Energy Error Bound Envelope: B_prefix(k, cloud_regime) for k in [1..24], tested as a Dynamic Horizon-Indexed Emergency Battery Reserve (EBR) trajectory in GAP19 Stage 2.
exact_evidence_supporting_recommendation: 1. Intra-day Deficit Timing: In 97.7% of 2024 origins, maximum cumulative solar shortfall occurs before horizon 24, peaking between horizons 14 and 17 (mean max shortfall 227.2 Wh/m2 vs final 24h net shortfall of 24.0 Wh/m2). A lumped 24h bound leaves afternoon hours vulnerable to battery exhaustion.

2. Battery Physical Integration: Battery state satisfies E_k = E_0 + sum_{t=1}^k (P_gen - P_load) dt. Microgrid deficits occur when prefix energy fails to meet prefix load; a prefix cumulative bound Delta E_prefix(k) matches battery storage state dynamics exactly.

3. Empirical Prefix Tractability: Prefix error std expands smoothly from 3.7 Wh/m2 at h=1 to 511.4 Wh/m2 at h=16, then plateaus at night, reflecting atmospheric physics without requiring pointwise hourly independence assumptions.

4. Explains Failure of Pointwise Relaxations: Forensics of L2-EXP-11 (NN adaptive q) and L2-EXP-12 (horizon risk budget) proved that uncoordinated hourly relaxations fail because they deplete the battery before afternoon deficit troughs. A prefix bound enforces energy conservation across all sub-horizons.

5. Zero GAP19 Architecture Impact: Can be implemented directly as a time-indexed EBR floor E_batt(k) >= EBR_baseline(k) + B_prefix(k) in GAP19 Stage 2. Adds zero decision variables, requires zero multi-scenario non-anticipativity constraints, and avoids the EXP-06 sensor-blocked physical upper envelope.
what_must_not_be_changed_yet: Production code in system/, EMS, router.py, and realization executor.
GAP19 MILP objective hierarchy, priorities, and solver tolerances.
Stage 8.1 / Candidate F model weights, features, and frozen artifact hashes.
Numerical physical envelope upper bound constants (no tuning of 80 W/m2 or diffuse floors until sensor authority is established).
Pre-registered governance files and test suites.
unresolved_assumptions: 1. Station Engine Fuel Curve Calibration: Linear fuel equation (5.0 L/h + 0.00025 L/Wh) remains an uncalibrated engineering prototype; exact physical Liter savings in the field remain unvalidated.

2. High-Zenith Low-Sun Diffuse Decomposition: Relative quantitative contributions of diffuse skylight, mountain terrain reflection, snow albedo, and pyranometer cosine error at Mount Nuolja remain unmeasured due to lack of DHI/DNI sensors (EXP-06).
3. Operational Replay Scope: Evaluated on 173 odd origins (semi-empirical replay fixture); performance under live real-time rolling telemetry remains an operational inference.
4. Historical Pre-2024 Evening Hours: Hours 19:00 to 23:00 UTC remain absent from the historical MEPS 18Z archive.
